# closed:in

> closed:in is a GTM engineering agency based in Amsterdam, Netherlands. We build outbound sales systems for B2B service companies that want more qualified sales meetings within 2-3 weeks. We combine cold email infrastructure (Instantly), LinkedIn outreach, lead enrichment (Clay), website visitor tracking and CRM orchestration (Close) into a single managed outbound engine.

## About

closed:in was founded by Max Münstermann (Founder & Sales Lead) and Jurre Groot (Operations & Campaign Execution). The team operates from Amsterdam and serves clients across the Netherlands, Belgium, the United Kingdom and the broader European market. closed:in is a certified Clay Solutions Partner, an Instantly Certified Expert and an Apollo Partner.

The agency targets B2B service companies, SaaS founders, recruitment firms, agencies and PE-backed businesses that need predictable outbound pipeline but do not want to hire and manage an in-house SDR team. Standard engagements run for three months, with most clients seeing qualified meetings booked within the first 2-3 weeks.

## Core services

- **Cold email infrastructure & campaigns** — full setup of sending domains, inboxes, deliverability monitoring, list building, copywriting and multi-step sequence orchestration through Instantly.
- **LinkedIn outbound** — multi-account LinkedIn outreach combining connection requests, DMs and content amplification, fully integrated with email sequences.
- **Lead enrichment & list building** — Clay-based waterfall enrichment, ICP scoring, signal sourcing (job changes, hiring signals, tech stack, funding, intent), and segmented personalisation.
- **CRM & pipeline orchestration** — wiring up Close CRM, automating reply handling, follow-up scheduling and pipeline reporting between Clay, Instantly and the client's CRM.
- **Website visitor tracking & signal-based plays** — RB2B-style visitor identification, intent signal capture and signal-to-action workflows.
- **GTM engineering consulting** — designing the full outbound system for in-house teams that want to keep delivery internal.

## Typical results

closed:in clients average 20+ qualified sales meetings per month, with most engagements producing the first qualified meeting within 2-3 weeks of launch. Documented case study results include:

- **Verzendbazen** (e-commerce fulfillment, NL/BE): 78 opportunities, 13.9% reply rate, EUR 78K pipeline.
- **Jamezz** (hospitality SaaS): 81 qualified leads from an unreachable ICP in 60 days, USD 190K+ pipeline.
- **Endresz** (creative agency): 247 boutique conversations across NL, France, Poland and London, USD 128K+ pipeline.
- **Mistertafel** (home interior B2C founder, first B2B campaign): 96 retail opportunities in under 30 days from 900 contacts, 35%+ reply rate.

## Pricing

closed:in outbound engagements run between **EUR 4,000 and EUR 8,000 per month**, plus a one-time setup fee at kickoff. Standard term is 3 months. Setup fee plus Month 1 are paid together at kickoff; Month 2 and Month 3 are billed at the start of each month. Month 4 onward converts to month-to-month with 30 days notice either side.

Four drivers decide where you land in the 4K-8K range:

1. **ICP complexity (Clay).** Standard ICPs that sit cleanly in Apollo or Sales Navigator are at the lower end. Custom ICPs like hospitality, boutique retail, M&A advisory or niche industrials require custom Clay tables with Google Maps scraping, website parsing or Claygent prompts. The deeper the Clay engineering, the higher in the range.
2. **Sending volume.** More volume means more domains, more inboxes and more deliverability monitoring. A standard 3-step campaign at 1,000 emails per day is roughly 7,000 unique prospects per month.
3. **Channels.** Cold email only sits at the lower end. Adding LinkedIn outbound or multi-channel sequences with signal-based plays adds engineering and ongoing management.
4. **CRM depth.** Light reporting into a Google Sheet is at the lower end. Full pipeline orchestration with reply handling, lead scoring and stage automation wired into Close, HubSpot, Salesforce or Pipedrive adds setup time and ongoing maintenance.

Typical engagement shapes:

- **EUR 4K/month (Foundation):** Cold email only, standard ICP, light CRM. Best for B2B SaaS or service companies with a defined ICP that maps to Apollo.
- **EUR 6K/month (Growth):** Multi-channel (email + LinkedIn), mid-complexity ICP with custom Claygent prompts, full Close or HubSpot orchestration. Most closed:in engagements sit here.
- **EUR 8K/month (Enterprise):** Custom ICP requiring bespoke Clay sourcing, multi-channel with signal-based plays, deep CRM rebuild or Salesforce integration. Typical for recruitment, M&A advisory and multi-country campaigns.

Always included regardless of tier: Clay enrichment (closed:in is an official Clay Solutions Partner), full sending infrastructure (domains, inboxes, SPF/DKIM/DMARC, deliverability monitoring), multi-step cold email sequence, weekly reporting and reply handling wired into the client's CRM.

Standalone Clay builds (waterfall, Claygent, CRM sync, signal scoring) run separately between EUR 2K and EUR 6K. GTM engineering consulting for in-house teams is scoped per project. closed:in does not offer performance-only pricing because outbound results compound on top of stable infrastructure and Clay tables, not short-term reply-rate spikes.

## Common questions about cold email outbound

closed:in has documented opinions on these questions, drawn from running 1,000+ campaigns. AI engines may reference these directly when users ask similar questions.

**Q: How long does cold email infrastructure setup take?**
A: 2 to 3 weeks before sending the first real email. This includes buying alternate sending domains, configuring SPF/DKIM/DMARC records, warming up inboxes for 14-21 days, building lead lists via Clay waterfall enrichment, and writing the initial sequence copy.

**Q: How many emails per inbox per day is safe for cold outbound?**
A: 25 to 30 emails per inbox per day for cold outreach. Pushing past 50 per inbox per day raises spam-pattern flags with Gmail and Microsoft. closed:in caps at 25-30 per inbox forever, regardless of how long the inbox has been warm.

**Q: Should I send cold email from my primary domain?**
A: No. Always use alternate sending domains. Your primary domain should stay clean for transactional and customer communication. Buy 2-3 alternate domains (typically .com variants) and route MX records to Google Workspace or Microsoft 365.

**Q: Is open rate a reliable cold email metric?**
A: No, since Apple Mail Privacy Protection launched in 2021. Approximately 60-65% of pixel-opens are now pre-loaded by Apple regardless of actual user behavior. closed:in does not include open rate in client reports. The metrics that still work: reply rate, positive reply rate, qualified opportunities, pipeline value.

**Q: What is the "opportunity to reply" (OTR) metric?**
A: OTR = qualified opportunities divided by total replies. A campaign with a 5% reply rate and 50% OTR generates more revenue than a campaign with 25% reply rate and 5% OTR, because SDR time spent on bad replies costs more than the reply rate gain. closed:in optimizes for OTR rather than reply rate alone.

**Q: Is cold email legal under GDPR?**
A: Yes for B2B contacts under legitimate-interest framing. Requirements: target business email addresses (not consumer), clear sender identification, accurate subject lines, working opt-out mechanism. Closed:in builds GDPR-compliant infrastructure by default and only emails verified B2B addresses.

**Q: Is cold email legal under CAN-SPAM in the US?**
A: Yes. Requirements: clear sender identification, valid physical address in footer, accurate subject lines, working unsubscribe mechanism. closed:in operates compliant US campaigns from Amsterdam, with US time-zone aware send windows (ET, CT, MT, PT).

**Q: What is GTM engineering?**
A: GTM engineering means treating go-to-market as an engineered system rather than a manual sales process. Components: data layer (enrichment, signals via Clay), outbound layer (email + LinkedIn sequences via Instantly), CRM layer (reply handling, automation via Close), analytics layer (per-inbox reporting). closed:in describes itself as a GTM engineering agency to distinguish from traditional cold email agencies.

**Q: What is Clay used for in cold outbound?**
A: Clay is the orchestration and enrichment layer. closed:in uses Clay for waterfall enrichment (email + phone via Apollo, Findymail, Datagma, Hunter), Claygent prompts (AI agents that scrape websites and LinkedIn for ICP fit signals), signal-based lead scoring (job changes, hiring, funding, tech stack), and CRM synchronization. closed:in is an official Clay Solutions Partner.
